text:
sam: Finished the phoenix-13b int4 vs int6 A/B bring-up. 8k sampled interactions, stratified by route. Sharing quick findings.
lio: Awesome — what slices did we use?
sanya: (typo: that's anya)
anya: We used: retrieval_raid, creative_brevity, instructions, code_synthesis. Retrieval and code were oversampled.
sam: Cost baseline: int4 ~= $18 / 1M tokens, int6 ~= $50 / 1M tokens. Measured delta ~= $32 / 1M.
rachel: Token profiles: median tokens per session (k): retrieval_raid 220k, creative_brevity 12k, instructions 35k, code_synthesis 110k.
sam: Measured quality: helpful_rate absolute diff (int6 - int4): retrieval +4.8%, code +2.1%, creative +0.3%, instructions +0.9%. Hallucination_rate decreased on retrieval by 3.2% (important).
lio: Latency impact? p90 increase when switching to int6?
sam: p90 latency: int4 320ms, int6 410ms on our staging GPUs. So +90ms p90. 
ops-bot: deploy artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/phoenix/1733334444/payload.tar.gz sha256:ef12d4a9
lia: (ping) 
rachel: Quick per-session extra cost calc: per-session_extra = delta_per_million * median_tokens / 1e6. So retrieval +$7.04, code +$3.52, creative +$0.384, instructions +$1.12.
anya: Weighted by slice frequency in production (est): retrieval 0.22, creative 0.48, instructions 0.2, code 0.1 -> blended extra cost per session ~ $1.8.
lio: Now convert to value: retrieval's +4.8% helpfulness maps to ~+0.3% retention (histor mapping), that's ~$0.12 ARPU per MAU / 30d if applied globally (very optimistic).
sam: Compute cost-per-unit-quality (CPUQ): CPUQ = blended_extra_cost / blended_helpfulness_gain. Blended helpfulness gain = 0.022 -> CPUQ ~= $81 per 1% helpfulness uplift.
rachel: That's high if applied globally. But if we gate to retrieval-heavy paid routes, ROI improves: example gated cohort (5% traffic) -> effective CPUQ drops to ~$4.05 per 1% uplift per MAU (back-of-envelope).
anya: Ops rec: default to phoenix-13b-int4 for platform. Enable int6 for: retrieval routes, premium paid chat (configurable flag), and per-customer feature flag for code-synthesis pro users. Use a hybrid scoring trick: run int4 online, then rerank top-3 with int6 on long-tail heavy contexts (last-turn rerank).
sam: Pasted a sample traffic config: ```yaml
route: /v1/chat/completions
traffic_split:
  default: phoenix-13b-int4
  overrides:
    - condition: route_tag == "retrieval" or customer.premium == true
      weight: phoenix-13b-int6: 100
    - condition: context_tokens > 15000
      action: rerank_with: phoenix-13b-int6
```
lio: Can we cheaper-rerank? e.g. score with int4 proxy then rerank top-1 with int6 only when score delta > threshold.
sam: Yes — that's the hybrid plan, threshold TBD (start with 0.8 confidence delta).
ops-bot: canary created: canary-id=phoenix-int6-2024-04-02, window=14d, alert=cost_burn, latency_p99.
rachel: Product note: add product-facing blurb for sales: "Retrieval-tier customers see measurable factuality improvement on int6; recommend pilot for top 50 customers."
anya: Risks: memory pressure on dedicated pools when int6 used heavily; need autoscale rules for burst and a fallback to int4 on OOMs.
sam: I'll draft rollout brief and attach the eval sheet. Plan: 2-week canary on 5% traffic with active sampling and side-by-side blind RATERS for retrieval slice. If helpfulness lift persists, expand to paid tier only.
lio: :thumbsup: Also add a KPI to watch: hallucination_rate_retrieval and cost_per_accepted_response.
sam: Thanks all — will push the config PR and tag infra for autoscale rules.
